s.g: (informal, chiefly Canada, Upper Midwestern US, New Zealand, Australia, UK, Ireland, South Africa, India, Hong Kong, Singapore, Commonwealth) Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.
s.t: Australia, Canada, India, Ireland, UK, informal
s.x: These hot dogs are pretty good, eh?

s.g: In isolation, a request for repetition or clarification of what has just been said.
s.x: —I've been studying Graphiurus murinus. —Eh? Studying what?

s.g: In isolation, expressing surprise or confusion.
s.x: —You're going to be a dad! —Eh? You're joking!

s.g: (chiefly Canada) An interjection used to ascertain the continued attention of someone addressed by the speaker.
s.x: I went to the restaurant, eh, but my friends didn't show up.

s.g: Expressing apathy or lack of enthusiasm; meh.
s.x:
—Do you feel like going out tonight?
—Eh, I don't know.

s.g: (informal, predicative only) Of mediocre quality; unremarkable.
(Singlish, usually impolite) Hey, oi; said to get someone's attention.
(MLE, MTE, regional African-American Vernacular, Chicano) an attention grabber
(informal, Internet slang) A greeting between friends (typically male) or display of approval.
(Caribbean, chiefly Trinidad and Tobago) Used to negate the following verb; (am/are/is/do/does) not.

ehc.f: (UK, education) Initialism of education, health, and care.

ehd.f: (veterinary medicine, agriculture) Initialism of epizootic hemorrhagic disease.

ehf.f: (medicine, virology) Initialism of Ebola hemorrhagic fever.

ehh.f: Alternative form of eh (a request for clarification)

ehic.f: Initialism of European Health Insurance Card.

s.g: (medicine) A tick-borne disease caused by infection with bacteria of the genus Ehrlichia.
